reviews.comment: One of the better professors for DiffEQ. Exams are very similar to the homework. The practice exams are helpful. However, he goes deep into theory and is sometimes hard to follow.
I stopped going to classes after a month cuz they barely helped and goes pretty deep into theory. There are pop quizzes so show up. Lenient grader so take if you want a good grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I didn't pay attention to a single lecture to be honest, he went to much into theory stuff and was hard to understand. I would study for his exams a few days before and get an A. Do the regular and training homework. He will let you know what is on exams. Go to class in case of surprise quizzes. Overall good pick for dif. eq. in my opinion.

Dr. Nekrashevych was a solid professor. His exams were noticeably easier than other profs, and his lectures were good enough. He would go really in depth into the theory at times, but the exams never went that deep. He was helpful in office hours and is overall a solid pick for diff eq.

This professor grades leniently and is knowledgeable. His lectures are sometimes hard to follow but you will understand the gist of what he is talking about and be well prepared for the exams as long as you understand how to do each homework question and read through the lecture slides he posts. If you put in any decent effort you will do well.

2 exams, weekly homework, and a final. His lectures were tough to follow in my opinion. After the first exam, I had to use almost entirely only outside resources to learn the content. He also goes very fast in lectures; when he does an example it's hard to learn when things are going so fast. The exams were similar to homework.

Very easy to get an A in as long as you use outside resources and focus on studying homeworks. My issue with him is that his lectures are messy and hard to follow along. If you want to understand linear algebra, do not take this professor. I ended with an A but I feel like I'm not taking anything out of this class for my other math classes.

Attending lectures does not help that much... The exams are just like the weekly homeworks, and he grades very leniently for both of those things. I attended maybe half of the lectures and learned everything else by doing the homeworks. The professor himself is very nice--I made a mistake when submitting my homework, and he let me submit it late.

Linear Algebra on its face is a moderately difficult subject. Professor Nekrashevych took that subject and made it 10x worse. I stopped attending lectures, because he chose to teach the subject entirely in theory, while the homework and exams were practical questions. The lectures were VERY confusing. His only redeeming quality is he graded easy.

Linear Algebra sucks, there's not many professors that will be completely outstanding, and Nekrashevych was a fairly good one on the list. He grades pretty leniently and is very understanding if you reach out to him. Just don't expect the lectures to be much help. Mainly focus on the textbook and the home works. Exams are just like the Homework.

He flies through lectures and it's difficult to keep up with what he's saying. He teaches right out of the textbook, which makes it easy to catch up. Doesn't give good feedback on homework, which there isn't much of. This class is heavy on arithmetic and its easy to make little cascading algebra mistakes, but he doesn't count off much for them.

The accent is okay to get through but the lectures are so over your head. It is very hard to keep track of and pay attention too. Homework is reasonably accessible, although some topics went rather than what was covered in the house, and grading was fair but getting feedback took a while. I wouldnt take again if I can help it

Weekly homework & 3 exams. Takes long to reply to emails. Honestly was praying for a C and ended up getting a B because everyone else did bad too and I think he was a little more lenient after the COVID situation. I would recommend taking someone else if you can. He did end up letting me redo two homeworks at the end of the semester when I asked.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class does get progressively more difficult, but he is very straightforward about what will be on the tests. Tests are highly computational and easy to make careless mistakes on. Thankfully he is a fair grader. Not many kids go to class because his lectures are more abstract and theoretical, but I found them helpful and enjoyed the class. Good prof

Has an accent, but while it is easy to discern what words are coming out of his mouth, it is impossible to understand what he is talking about. He spends every lecture covering the board in equations and theorems that will never be used on any problems and does not explain what they do. After the first test the class becomes impossible do not take.
reviews.ratingTags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Has an accent but it is not hard to understand. Homework is assigned every week & you have 1 week to do it. His test are similar to the review handouts he places on his website, but do not ONLY use those to study, refer back to the HW too. HW is all on the interweb. After the first exam, things get a lot harder. Try to take a different professor.

He has a very thick accent and spends most of the class writing theorems and equations on the board without explaining what they do. Exams are way harder than the content seen in lectures and homeworks. Do not take his class if you are not ready to learn all the topics by yourself.
reviews.ratingTags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY
